title: A Stormy Week of Art in NYC
summary: Reviews on major exhibitions at the New Museum, Guggenheim, and MoMA PS1, what it takes to get a fair union contract, and finding joy in the history of concrete.

title: Four Artists Win MacArthur “Genius” Grants
summary: Christine Sun Kim, Rodney McMillian, Vincent Valdez, and Chip Thomas are among the 20 recipients of the $800,000 prize.

title: The Breathtaking Sight of Ancient Rome's Largest Surviving Wall Mosaic
summary: Beneath the ruins of the Baths of Trajan, a giant mosaic and unusual fresco remind us of the continual discovery of the wondrous: Rome’s ongoing lesson.

title: How Are Artists Affording Pet Care?
summary: From $1,600 dental bills to $16,000 emergency procedures, artists and culture workers weigh in on the rising cost of caring for their closest companions.

title: Four Artists Exploring Sustainable Alternatives to Synthetic Art Supplies
summary: In “Source Materials: A Bioart Exhibit,” artists share their visions for a future of art-making rooted in local ecosystems, scientific inquiry, and collaboration.

title: Unions Reach Tentative Agreements at Brooklyn Museum and American Folk Art Museum
summary: Potentially averting strike action, both unions are set to vote on ratifying the tentative agreements with their respective museums starting today, September 29.

title: Kehinde Wiley Requests to Buy Back Painting Removed by State Department
summary: Trump officials removed the work from an embassy in the Dominican Republic in August, labeling it "woke."

title: Jean Shin Creates Her Own Anti-War Camouflage
summary: Highlighting patterns of war and migration, her installation "Tidal Crossing" is the latest artist intervention at the Brooklyn Army Terminal.

title: Whitney Museum Workers Declare Strike
summary: The union prepares for work stoppage ahead of the Lichtenstein show. Plus, Teresa Margolles distills the language of violence at MoMA PS1.

title: Teresa Margolles and the Violence We Breathe
summary: Her MoMA PS1 exhibition raises the question: What exactly does formal restraint accomplish in an age of violent excess?

title: Art in Odd Places Participants Seek Utopia Under Dark Clouds
summary: The public art festival’s 21st edition unfolded across 14th Street throughout the nor’easter this past weekend.

title: Activists Unveil Quilt Honoring Thousands Disappeared by ICE in Minnesota
summary: The Stolen Neighbors Quilt features 11,000 hand-stitched squares in an indictment of violence against immigrants and a “call for political courage.”

title: The Rough-and-Ready Brilliance of Barbara Hammer’s “Nitrate Kisses”
summary: Newly restored in 4K, the film feels prescient as groups are once again being scapegoated for public health crises and financial instability.

title: Kenzi Shiokava Did It for the Love of It
summary: He modeled what a life in art can amount to without acclaim, celebrity, money, and all the other trappings we tell artists are required.

title: Whitney Museum Union Sets Strike Date Ahead of Major Roy Lichtenstein Show
summary: “We’d rather be working and doing our jobs, but our wages are untenable for making ends meet in New York City,” said the union's chairperson.
